newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait to sell 90 mln Gulf Bank shares.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait to sell 90 mln Gulf Bank shares.

text.p: Kuwait plans to sell 90 million of its 97 million shares in Gulf Bank in a two-stage privatisation, the Kuwait News Agency said on Thursday.

Kuwait Investment Authority (KIA), the state investment arm which holds 12.4 percent of the bank's issued shares, plans to sell 30 million shares at a minimum of 510 fils ($1.70) each in a public auction on January 16, the official agency said.
Gulf Bank share closed at 510 fils on Wednesday. There are 1,000 fils to the dinar.
Another 60 million shares will be offered in a public subscription at a later stage, at a price yet to be determined, the agency said.
Gulf Bank, one of the Gulf Arab state's six commercial banks, made a 15.3 million dinars net profit in the first half of 1996 compared to 12.3 million in the same period of 1995.

The sale is part of Kuwait's plan to shed state holdings in about 60 local firms and public services such as electricity, water and telecommunications. The plan, announced after the 1991 Gulf War, is under the supervision of KIA.
Proceeds from privatisations, which started in 1994, have so far totalled some 650 million dinars from the sale of stakes in 17 companies.
Only nationals of Kuwait and fellow Gulf Arab states -- Saudi Arabia, Oman, Qatar, Bahrain and the United Arab Emirates -- can trade shares of local firms.
